newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee slides on NY losses, CFTC news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee slides on NY losses, CFTC news.

text.p: Robusta futures retreated further on Monday afternoon after sharp New York losses led by fund selling, but some positions still managed to close off the day's lows.
Sentiment was also dented by the latest U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders report, which showed a large increaase in speculative or non-commercial long positions. Traders termed the report as bearish.
The spot December on the New York futures led losses on fund liquidation as well as stop-loss and arbitrage selling early in the session.
"London is just following New York," said one trader.
"The funds are getting out of the December contract ahead of the first notice day on November 19 and I don't think they want to be long with it come next week," he said.
By the finish, benchmark January was $29 down at $1,432 after falling to a low of $1,422.
The second-position contract had gapped $11 lower at the open, but later rose to touch the day's high of $1,459 towards the midsession recess on arbitrage buying.
All eyes are now focused on coffee grading and certified stock figures due after the close of New York trading.
There had been no coffee pending grading or recertification in New York in past weeks and traders said they had not heard of large volumes of fresh arrivals.
There was some talk that about 1,500 bags were pending grading, but one trader said the volume was not big enough to scare the market.
Traders said news emerging from a weekend meeting of the Association of Producing Countries (ACPC) in Costa Rica had no immediate impact.
"They didn't say anything, did they?" said one.
The ACPC, in a release, made no mention of export volumes and highlighted the chairman's power to call extraodinary meetings if the situation merited such action.

On Monday, ACPC secretary-general Robeiro Oliveira told Reuters at the Sintercafe coffee week in Costa Rica that the group was not going to relax its export limit programme even though prices had been trending up.
